audit_findings.title: Equity stakes may be double counted through both earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.041 billion bridge addition and $1.212 billion pretax 2025 investment gain; dividends and equity-method results unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Investment gains, dividends, and equity-method earnings can increase anchor OE while the underlying investments are also added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Miscellaneous, net primarily includes employee benefit plans net periodic cost, charitable contributions, our share of our equity method investments' results, dividend income from our equity investments and foreign exchange gains/(losses).
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that investment returns entered reported earnings and that $4.041 billion of stakes was separately added to value. It does not establish whether the OE calculation removed all corresponding returns. Retention of even a meaningful portion could materially overstate value because the bear case exceeds the market price by only $2.16 per share.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 net income to the $3.9115 billion OE anchor line by line; remove after-tax fair-value gains, dividends, and equity-method results attributable to bridge-added stakes, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may undercharge the fleet reinvestment required immediately after 2025
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $1.0 billion gross increase from $4.499 billion of 2025 capex to approximately $5.5 billion expected for 2026; $27.6 billion of aircraft commitments at 2026-06-30
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated sustainable maintenance-capex charge inflates anchor OE and every forecast and terminal cash flow grown from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Our expected 2026 capital spend of approximately $5.5 billion, which may vary depending on financing decisions, will be primarily for aircraft, including deliveries and advance deposit payments, as well as fleet modifications and technology enhancements.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not establish how much of the elevated spending is replacement rather than growth capex, so the error itself remains unresolved. It is nevertheless material: only about a $122 million recurring OE reduction would erase the bear case's $2.16-per-share premium to market, far below the approximately $1.0 billion gross spending increase.
audit_findings.action: Build a delivery-by-delivery fleet schedule separating replacement, required modification and technology spending from capacity growth; normalize maintenance capex in the anchor and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 tax burden is not a sustainable terminal tax rate
audit_findings.magnitude: 3.9-5.9 percentage-point gap between the 19.1% 2025 effective rate and the filed 23%-25% 2026 projection; applying that spread to $4.973 billion of pretax income after removing the $1.212 billion investment gain indicates $194-$293 million before further tax-base adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Using the unusually low 2025 tax burden raises after-tax anchor OE and permanently capitalizes that benefit through forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Excluding the mark-to-market results, we project our annual effective tax rate to be between 23% and 25% for 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary nature of the 2025 rate is demonstrated by the valuation-allowance activity, loss-carryforward usage and management's higher projected rate. Whether the valuation normalized taxes is not demonstrated. The indicated annual difference exceeds the approximately $122 million OE reduction needed to eliminate the bear-case premium.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct normalized cash taxes on operating pretax income after removing investment items and temporary valuation-allowance effects; incorporate NOL exhaustion and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Sale-leaseback gains may inflate recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring sale-leaseback gains can increase the OE anchor while the resulting recurring lease expense remains in future earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in other operating expense primarily resulted from gains from several sale-leaseback transactions and lower irregular operations expense in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that several sale-leaseback gains reduced 2025 operating expense, but supplies no amount and the OE adjustment record does not show whether they were removed. The direction is adverse, but the supplied record cannot establish whether the amount is large enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the transaction-level 2025 gain and proceeds schedule, remove each after-tax gain from OE, confirm proceeds were excluded from operating OE, and rerun if the recurring adjustment is significant.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retiree benefits may require more cash than the earnings charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.217 billion underfunded obligation; $466 million of 2025 employer contributions versus $328 million expense, a computed $138 million excess cash charge; expected payments of $480-$500 million annually through 2030
audit_findings.mechanism: If OE retains accrual benefit expense instead of the higher cash funding burden, OE is overstated; alternatively, an uncaptured beneficiary claim belongs in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Benefit payments for these obligations are expected to be approximately $500 million on an annual basis over the next five years.
audit_findings.explanation: The excess cash burden is demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the OE calculation captured it or whether the $2.258 billion pension surplus is legally and economically available to offset the unfunded plans. Capitalizing the $138 million 2025 gap at the bear-case OE multiple implies about $1.64 billion, or $2.45 per share, enough to eliminate the $2.16 bear-case premium.
audit_findings.action: Trace benefit expense, employer cash payments and cash-flow adjustments into OE; obtain plan-level restrictions on the pension surplus, then either normalize OE for excess payments or add a properly netted bridge claim and rerun.

audit_findings.title: The fuel purchasing card may be an omitted financing claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.1 billion, equal to $1.64 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding gross cash without offsetting a separately reported monthly-settled financing obligation can overstate the equity bridge if the obligation is neither included in debt nor captured through OE financing costs.
audit_findings.evidence: At both December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had $1.1 billion outstanding on this purchasing card and the activity was classified as a financing activity in our cash flows statement.
audit_findings.explanation: The $1.1 billion obligation is separately reported, remained outstanding at June 2026 and is classified as financing. A full bridge deduction would reduce bear value from $82.33 to about $80.69 per share, still approximately $0.52 above the $80.17 market price; base value would remain about $93.25. Standing alone, it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 2026 card balance is excluded from the $13.952 billion debt figure and not netted from cash; if omitted, rerun the bridge with a $1.1 billion offset and document fees and monthly settlement mechanics.
